title: Steve Jobs on failure, Apple's lost lead, and bringing a liberal arts view to computers (1996 Terry Gross interview)
summary: In 1996, after Pixar's Toy Story success, Jobs reflects on being ousted from Apple and not fearing failure, why Apple lost its ten-year lead by ceasing to innovate, and how Apple's real contribution was a liberal arts view of computing. He also describes a bottoms-up culture where great hires tell you what to do, and says work and life are the same thing.

principles.text: Don't be afraid to fail; you never achieve what you want without falling on your face a few times.
principles.quote: you never achieve what you want without falling on your face a few times in the process of getting there. I’ve tried to not be afraid to fail

principles.text: After a painful setback, march forward and learn from it rather than becoming protective.
principles.quote: That was a very painful time, but you just march forward, and you try to learn from it.

principles.text: Stopping innovation squanders even a ten-year lead; differentiation evaporates and cost-cutting won't cure it.
principles.quote: The problem at Apple was that they stopped innovating.

principles.text: Outside the mainstream you must be far better, because customers take a risk and want a bigger reward.
principles.quote: Apple has to be 50 percent or 100 percent better, because when you buy something that is out of the mainstream a little bit, you take a risk

principles.text: Technology should marry with the liberal arts: bring beauty, typography and ease of use to everyone, not only geeks.
principles.quote: Our goal was to bring a liberal arts perspective and a liberal arts audience to what had traditionally been a very geeky technology and a very geeky audience.

principles.text: Hire truly great people and give them room; let them tell you what to do, and let ideas come from anywhere.
principles.quote: we hired truly great people and gave them the room to do great work. A lot of companies—I know it sounds crazy—but a lot of companies don’t do that. They hire people to tell them what to do. We hired people to tell us what to do.
